Methyl Tertiary Butyl Ether (MTBE) is a colorless, flammable liquid that
possess high affinity for water. Ideally, MTBE is employed as an extractant
and solvent in various chemical industries. Around 90 percent of MTBE produced
globally is utilized as an octane booster in gasoline. Although Ethanol is
regarded as its eco-friendly alternative, but MTBE is still being preferred
over it on the back of its lower volatility, easy transportability, and ideal
performance in reduction of formaldehyde and benzene in gasoline. In addition
to its use as an oxygenator, MTBE is also used to produce Isobutylene with
high purity. MTBE is commercially produced by the reaction of Methanol and
Isobutylene in either a mixed gas-liquid or liquid phase reactor with an
acidic ion exchange resin. The reaction proceeds at a pressure of 20 bar and
at a temperature between 50-90 degree Celsius. The reaction mixture is then
subjected to distillation to manufacture high purity MTBE. Although, several
innovations are being made to upgrade the technology for producing a gasoline
blendstock with high octane paraffin.

Nylon Tire Yarn (NTY) is a widely used as reinforcement in tyre to provide
them strength and durability. Around 97% of the global NTY produce is used in
manufacturing tyres used in motorcycles, scooters, light commercial vehicles
(LMVs), heavy commercial vehicles (HCVs) and off the road (OTR) vehicles. The
production method involves the passage of dried Nylon chips into a melt
spinning machines which are then made to enter the spinneret to form a yarn of
different densities as per specifications. Fibres of different length and
thickness are made using holes of different sizes and varying ejection speed.
The filaments produced are coated with water & oil to ensure dimensional
stability followed by optimum quenching and solidification which offers
desired tensile strength, elasticity and shrinkage characteristics under
requisite heating. The yarn thus formed is further stretched multiple times to
its original length to ensure that macromolecules lie parallel to the fibre
length for full strength. Nylon tire yarn can be used for manufacturing tire
cords fabric using processes like twisting, weaving, and dipping of several
fibers.

Paraffin wax is soft colourless solid mixture of hydrocarbon, which is
obtained from petroleum or coal. This hydrocarbon mixture usually contains
large compounds between C20 to C40 chains and remains solid at room
temperature. Despite of its solid nature, it has a low melting point of around
36°C and boiling point of around 370°C. Paraffin wax is produced by feedstock

separated which is called de-oiling. After a successful first step, the
product is further treated for its odour and colour. Paraffin wax has wide
range of applications, in industries Paraffin wax is further treated to change
its crystalline structure, viscosity and other functional properties. Other
applications of Paraffin wax include making candles, wax carving for moulding,
anticaking agent in fertilisers, making crayons, coating on paper, food
additives etc.

meet desirable quality standards. Polyester Staple Fiber (PSF) has emerged as
the fastest growing fiber amongst all types of man-made fibers possessing
appearance similar to cotton or wool fiber when baled. Technically, PSF is
obtained by co-polymerization of PTA and MEG feedstocks. The polymer thus
obtained is melt spun and the bundle of continuous filaments thus obtained by
melt spinning is called tow. The tow is further made to undergo processes like
drawing, crimping, spin finish and then cut into fixed lengths to get cut
fibers, almost equal in length known as PSF. PSF is widely used for spinning
yarns and making geotextiles, and certain PSF is known in the industry as
"fiber for fill," because it is primarily used as a polyester fiberfill. PSF
is also widely used as stuffing in sleeping bags, mattresses, ski jackets,
comforters, cushions, sofas, pillows, and furniture. Polyester staple is
generally spun to make polyester spun yarn, which is then knitted or weaved
into fabrics. To fight the global issue of reduction of non-biodegradable
wastes, there has been increased focus of the economies towards manufacturing
Polyester Staple Fiber (PSF) from recycled non-biodegradable pet bottle waste.

Toluene Diisocyanate (TDI) is a highly reactive aromatic isocyanate, primarily
synthesized to produce Polyurethane (PU) foams which is further utilized for
mattresses, upholstery and automotive. In addition to PU elastomers and
coatings, TDI is also utilized in adhesives, paints, rigid foams and concreate
sealants. With anticipated increment in demand for Polyurethanes in various
end-use industries, demand for TDI is anticipated to observe a healthy growth
in the coming years. Being a relatively denser compound, TDI interacts with
water in an exothermic reaction forming carbon dioxide and insoluble polyurea.
Commercial production of TDI is mainly achieved by Nitration of Toluene to
Dinitrotoluene, the reaction is proceeded by catalytic hydrogenation of the
former compound to Toluene Diamine (TDA) which is further dissolved in an
inert solvent and reacted with phosgene to finally process the intermediate
into crude TDI. Another method to manufacture TDI is via carbonylation with
o-dichlorobenzene straight from dinitrotoluene.

Butadiene (BD) is flammable, colorless gas with a mild aromatic odor. It is
readily soluble in alcohol and ether, insoluble in water and readily
polymerizes in the presence of oxygen. One of the most important use of
Butadiene is in the manufacture of synthetic rubber such as styrene-butadiene
rubber (SBR), nitrile butadiene rubbers (NBR), polybutadiene rubber (PBR)
(Cis-polybutadiene and trans-polybutadiene) and other elastomeric formulations
with specific properties. PBR and SBR accounts for nearly 55% of the global
Butadiene demand. Other large consuming segments include Acrylonitrile
Butadiene Styrene (ABS), Polychloroprene, and Adiponitrile (feedstock for
Nylon -6,6). Butadiene is also used extensively for various polymerization
reactions during plastics manufacturing. Butadiene is commonly produced via
two routes - (1) as a by-product during production of Ethylene and Propylene
production wherein the crude C4 stream is isolated from steam cracking process
and is fed to extract Butadiene from the other C4s via extractive
distillation. (2) by dehydrogenation of n-Butane or n-Butene which are
obtained from steam crackers or C4 refinery streams. Leading licensors of the
production technology for Butadiene include-Shell, BASF and Nippon-Zeon.

Isopropyl alcohol (IPA), also known as Isopropanol, is a clear, colorless
liquid, possessing an alcoholic odor. It is a medium evaporating low-cost
solvent, possessing complete miscibility with most solvents. Based on
applications, IPA has several grades specially selected on the basis of purity
and odor. It has proven microbial, anti-bacterial, anti-infectant properties
making it suitable to be used in the cosmetics and toiletries. It is also
widely used as a low-cost solvent in many industries such as pharmaceuticals,
coatings and inks, specialty chemicals and as an extractant. Some important
chemical derivatives manufactured from IPA include methyl isobutyl ketone
(MIBK), isopropylamines and isopropyl esters. IPA can be produced either from
Propylene, as a by-product from the operations of a naphtha cracker, from
acetone, or as a by-product from producing phenol. Two main routes are used to
produce IPA commercially. The traditional method involves indirect hydration
of refinery-grade propylene (RGP) using sulfuric acid to form isopropyl
sulfate, which is then hydrolyzed with steam to form sulfuric acid and IPA.
Another route is the direct hydration of chemical grade (90-99%) Propylene,
without using sulfuric acid. Small amount of IPA is also produced by the
hydrogenation of Acetone in aqueous medium. However, this process is only
suitable where excess Acetone is available.

n-Hexane has the chemical formula of C 6 H 14 /CH3(CH2)5CH3. n-hexane is a
highly volatile, colourless liquid that is miscible with most organic solvents
and is less soluble in water. With oxidising materials such as liquid
chlorine, concentrated oxygen, and sodium hypochlorite, n-Hexane can interact
vigorously. The refining of crude oil produces n-hexane. Regulated fractional
distillation and other refinery-based processes segregate hydrocarbons within
specific boiling point ranges to produce n-hexane from petroleum mixtures. In

Chloroform (CHCL3), also known as trichloromethane, is a colorless, non-
flammable liquid, possessing vapor weight more than air. Chloroform possesses
a sweet, ether like odor and is insoluble in water. Chloroform is mainly used
to produce hydrochlorofluorocarbon-22 (HCFC-22) and Polytetrafluoroethylene
(PTFE) polymers. Increasing demand for HCFC's for use in refrigerants and
skyrocketing demand for fluoropolymers in the transportation, electrical &
electronics, medical, food processing etc. sectors will facilitate the growth
of the global Chloroform market in the forecast period. In addition to its
versatile industrial uses, Chloroform is also consumed as a solvent in pharma
industries and as an anesthetic in medicinal procedures to relax from pain.
Chloroform is commonly manufactured by the reaction of Methyl Chloride in the
presence of chlorine and is produced as a coproduct with methylene chloride.
Chloroform was initially produced by the chlorination of methane, producing
hydrogen chloride as the by-product, thereby posing a major challenge among
the producers. To resolve this issue, several companies across the globe have
started conducting absorption of the released acid over chloromethanes and
methyl chloride.

Tetrahydrofuran (THF), also known as Oxolane, is an organic compound having
transparent liquid appearance at room temperature. THF is a polar versatile
solvent which can be mixed in water and have lower viscosity. There are
several methods available to produce THF including a traditional one which is
not feasible to be used these days. One commercial method is the Reppe
synthesis. In this process 1,4-butanediol is dehydrogenated in the presence of
acid catalyst to yield THF. Another less popular method is hydroformylation of
allyl alcohol. Some manufacturers like DuPont have their own method to produce
THF, DuPont uses n-butane for the production. THF has multiple industrial
applications like it is widely used as solvent for polymer, resins, fat oils,
protective coatings etc. In addition, it is utilised in paints, adhesives,
coating, pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, making polyurethane spandex etc.

Non-woven fabrics are flat, porous sheets or web structures made from staple
fiber (short) and continuous fiber (long), bonded together into cohesive
fabrics by using mechanical, thermal, solvent treatment or chemical force.
Contrary to the traditional materials, like cotton, linen, wool, and silk;
production of Non-Woven fabric does not require special weaving or knitting.
Non-woven fabrics are used in a number of industries. In the healthcare
industry, non-woven fabrics are used for making isolation gowns, surgical
scrubs, and in packaging applications. In the carpeting industry, they are
used for carpet backing and in the fashion industry these are used for making
insulation and protection clothing, industrial workwear, chemical defense
suits, shoes parts, etc. Different type of Non-woven Fabrics are available
based on the method in which fibers are bonded together. Various production
methods include mechanical bonding (fiber entanglement), chemical bonding
(fibers are chemically bound using glue-like compounds), or thermal bonding
(where heat is used to melt the fibers together).  Spun melt is a generic term
used to describe the Non-woven webs manufactured directly from thermoplastic
polymers. The product under consideration i.e., Polypropylene (PP) grade Non-
Woven Fabric uses PP granules as the raw material which are extruded into
filaments through spinnerets which are then attenuated through pair of hot
cylinders acting as a bonding agent.

Acrylate esters, are the derivatives of Acrylic Acid, used as the key raw
material for thousands of polymer formulations. These are prepared by
esterification reaction between Acrylic Acid and different alcohol feedstocks.
Major downstream industries for Acrylate Esters include paints, viscosity
adhesives, acrylic gums, acrylic textiles, etc. Although a wide variety of
Acrylate Esters can be manufactured, our evaluation is restricted to Butyl and
Ethyl Acrylate as they are of the greatest commercial significance. Ethyl
acrylate can be manufactured through several industrial techniques. The most
prominent method involves reacting together Acrylonitrile and Ethanol using
Sulphuric Acid as the catalyst. Additionally, manufacturers may also use
phenolic type inhibitors, manganese, or cerium salts to catalyze its
production. Acetylene, carbon monoxide and ethanol may also be used as a
precursor in Ethyl Acrylate production. Ethyl acrylate is used in the
manufacture of water-based latex paints and adhesives, textile coatings,
leather finish resins, and for manufacturing Acrylic fibers. Butyl acrylate
which can be commonly produced via direct esterification of Acrylic Acid with
n-Butanol is widely used to produce adhesives, emulsifying agent, coatings,
water treatment, paper chemicals, and modifying agent for fiber and textile,
leather treatment agent and many more. Acrylate Esters are also widely used as
important feedstocks for chemical synthesis as they readily undergo addition
reactions with many organic and inorganic compounds.

Water soluble fertilizers is a class of fertilizers that are incorporated in
plants after thorough dissolution in water. The addition of WSF often supports
double or triple the normal yield of the crop. The agricultural sector is the
key consumer of water-soluble fertilizers. Due to their rapid impact, ease of
application and better coverage, Water Soluble Fertilizers are preferred over
conventional chemical fertilizers. These can also be applied more frequently
than granular fertilizers, therefore their usage can be varied as per their
requirement and availability. Being readily soluble in water, Water Soluble
Fertilizers (WSF) facilitate easy fertigation by releasing essential nutrients
at the root of the plants from where they are readily absorbed and transported
to the entire plant body. The key fertilizers falling under this category are:
Urea Phosphate, Sulphate of potash, Calcium Nitrate, Potassium Nitrate, Mono
Potassium Phosphate, Mono Ammonium Phosphate etc. Ever growing demand for
agricultural products is the key reason driving the demand for Water Soluble
fertilizers across the globe. However, growing awareness for organic farming
may limit the use of Water-Soluble Fertilizers in longer terms.

Potassium Carbonate is an inorganic compound. Its industrial name is Carbonate

soluble in water but insoluble in ethanol, acetone, and alcohol. It has viable
applications in the production of soap and glass. Potassium Carbonate is
commercially produced by the electrolysis of potash (potassium chloride) using

results in the formation of potassium bicarbonate which on calcination forms
potassium carbonate. Apart from soap and glass, Potassium Carbonate has
applications as drying agent, buffering agent and as a fire suppressant. In
its aqueous form, potassium chloride is used to remove carbon dioxide from
ammonia production synthesis gas in the fertilizer industry.

Propylene (C3H6), or Propene is a colorless, three carbon hydrocarbon with a
naturally pungent smell. At room temperature, Propylene exists as an extremely
flammable gas which becomes a liquid under pressure. It is the key chemical
building block for a wide range of chemicals and petrochemicals after
Ethylene. There are three grades of propylene- polymer grade (having minimum
purity of 99.5 per cent), chemical grade (having minimum purity of 93-94 per
cent), and refinery grade (with a purity of around 60-70 per cent). More than
half of the Propylene consumed globally is used for the production of
polypropylene (PP), a polymer popularly used for films and packaging
applications and a key material for plastic parts used across various
industries such as the automotive, textiles and many others. Other important
PP derivatives are Acrylonitrile (ACN), Propylene Oxide (PO), Oxo-alcohols,
Cumene and Acrylic Acid. The global Propylene industry is particularly complex
because of various methods of production and variety of end uses it serves.
Propylene is generally produced as a byproduct from the steam cracking of
liquid petrochemical feedstocks such as naphtha and LPG, and from residual
gases released in fluid catalytic cracking (FCC) units in refineries.
Propylene is also produced via on-purpose technologies such as propane
dehydrogenation (PDH), hydrodealkylation (HDA) of toluene, toluene
disproportionation (TDP) and metathesis. Being strongly tied to several
commodity petrochemicals, the overall Propylene consumption is strongly linked
to the general economic conditions and the expansion of polymer and
petrochemical industries across the globe.

n-Heptane is a straight chain alkane having a chemical formula of C7H16. It is
principally derived from crude oil and is highly volatile in nature. n-Heptane
is a clear, colourless liquid with an odour similar to petroleum. It cannot be
dissolved in water because it reacts violently with water. It is miscible with
ethyl alcohol, acetone, benzene, chloroform, and petroleum ether; soluble in
carbon tetrachloride; very soluble in ethanol. n-Heptane can be manufactured
from petroleum fractional distillation accompanied by rectification. It is
also obtained as a by-product from naphtha cracking. It is used in various
industries such as adhesives, paints & coatings, ink printing, pharmaceuticals
etc. Due to its hydrocarbon chemical composition, which liberate large
quantities of heat energy during hydrocarbon combustion, heptane is a perfect
fuel source for pressurised, outdoor liquid fuel. Apart from its use in engine
fuels, n- Heptane is mainly used as an extraction solvent in the processing of
vegetable oils. In addition, higher utilization of n-Heptane for different
applications has fueled the growth of the plastic & polymer industry, which in
turn is rising the worldwide consumer demand for n-Heptane.

Hydrobromic Acid is a colourless or light-yellow liquid formed by the
combination of a single atom of hydrogen and bromine. It has a boiling point
of 120˚C and melting point -110˚C. It is synthesized by dissolving gaseous
hydrogen bromide (48%) in water (62%). Due to its catalytic properties,
Hydrobromic Acid is used in extraction of most of the metals. Hydrobromic acid
is also used to manufacture organic or inorganic bromides such as Calcium
Bromide, Sodium Bromide and Zinc Bromide. Sodium Bromide is used in medical
industry to make anticonvulsant, hypnotic, and sedative. Calcium bromide is
used in food industry as preservative whereas Zinc bromide is used in
automobile industry to manufacture zinc batteries.  Even after being highly
corrosive in nature, Hydrobromic Acid cannot be replaced as a catalyst in the
industries, that creates abundant opportunities for its market growth.

Glycerine is also known as glycerol is a transparent, scentless, and viscous

in other chemical industries.

Alkyl Amines industry is an oligopoly with two-three producers catering to the

globally among the top six players having a greater hold of the global Alkyl

Polyethylene Terephthalate is one of the most important thermoplastic polymer

used in flexible electrical packaging applications. The product can be used in

Nitrile Butadiene Rubber (NBR), also known as Buna-N, is a synthetic rubber
copolymer consisting of acrylonitrile (ACN) and butadiene (BD) monomers. It is
a versatile elastomer with excellent oil resistance and mechanical properties,
making it widely used in various industries.



**The structure of NBR can be represented as follows:**

**  
**

**[-CH2-CH(CN)-]m [-CH=CH-CH2-]n**



In this structure, Acrylonitrile (ACN) units represented  by (-CH2-CH(CN)-)
and Butadiene (BD) units represented by (-CH=CH-CH2-), the "m" and "n"
represent the number of repeating units of acrylonitrile and butadiene,
respectively, and the brackets indicate that these units repeat throughout the
polymer chain.



**Product Specific Details**



**CAS No:** |  9003-18-3  
---|---  
**HS Code:** |  400259  
**Grade:** |  **AR content- 36%-43%, 36%-50%, 18%-40%, 18%-40%, 33%-38%,41%-66%**  
**Contract Size:** |  50-70 MT  
**Packaging Type:** |  Bags  
  


NBR is produced through a process called emulsion polymerization. The
monomers, acrylonitrile, and butadiene, are mixed with a water-based emulsion
and other additives such as emulsifiers and catalysts. The emulsion is then
heated and agitated to initiate the polymerization reaction. As the reaction
progresses, the monomers polymerize, forming long chains of repeating units.

The acrylonitrile component in NBR provides the rubber with its excellent oil
resistance, chemical resistance, and thermal stability. It also contributes to
its high tensile strength and abrasion resistance. The butadiene component, on
the other hand, enhances the rubber's elasticity and low-temperature
flexibility.



The percentage of acrylonitrile in the copolymer can vary, typically ranging
from 18% to 50%. Higher acrylonitrile content results in improved oil
resistance but reduced low-temperature flexibility. Conversely, lower
acrylonitrile content improves low-temperature performance but reduces oil
resistance. The desired acrylonitrile content is determined based on the
specific application requirements.



In addition to its inherent properties, NBR can be further modified with
fillers, plasticizers, curing agents, and other additives to enhance specific
characteristics such as flame resistance, electrical conductivity, or improved
processability during manufacturing.

Polybutadiene Rubber (PBR) is a synthetic rubber polymer with a structure
primarily composed of butadiene monomers. It is produced through the
polymerization of butadiene, which is a hydrocarbon compound containing four
carbon atoms and two double bonds.

PBR is classified as a homopolymer, meaning it consists of repeating units of
the same monomer (butadiene) in its polymer chain. The polymerization process
allows for the formation of long chains of butadiene units linked together,
resulting in the formation of a solid rubbery material.



One of the key characteristics of PBR is its high degree of cis-1,4 structure.
The cis configuration refers to the spatial arrangement of the butadiene
monomers along the polymer chain, where the side methyl groups are on the same
side of the chain. This arrangement gives PBR its unique properties, such as
excellent resilience, low rolling resistance, and high elasticity.



PBR exhibits a wide range of physical and mechanical properties that can be
tailored based on the polymerization conditions, such as temperature,
catalysts, and reaction time. By adjusting these parameters, manufacturers can
produce different grades of PBR with specific characteristics suited for
various applications.



The polymerization of PBR can be controlled to achieve different levels of
polymerization, resulting in variations in molecular weight and polymer chain
length. These factors influence properties like tensile strength, elongation,
and processability.

SBR is a thermoplastic elastomer, which means it exhibits both elastic and
plastic properties. It can be processed like a thermoplastic material at
elevated temperatures, allowing it to be molded or extruded into various
shapes. However, it also possesses elastic behaviour, enabling it to recover
its original shape after deformation.



The properties of SBR can be further modified by incorporating various
additives during the polymerization process or during subsequent compounding.
These additives can include reinforcing agents like carbon black or silica,
plasticizers, antioxidants, and vulcanization agents. Carbon black, in
particular, is commonly added to improve the strength and abrasion resistance
of SBR.

The chemical structure of SBR can be represented as:



**[-(CH2-CH=C(CH3)-CH2-C6H5-)m-(-(CH2-CH=CH-CH=CH2-)n-]x**

**  
**

In this representation, "(CH2-CH=C(CH3)-CH2-C6H5-)" represents the styrene
unit, and "(CH2-CH=CH-CH=CH2-)" represents the butadiene unit. The subscripts
"m" and "n" represent the number of repeating units of styrene and butadiene,
respectively, and "x" represents the number of polymer chains.

polymer, while the butadiene units contribute to its elasticity and

Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene (ABS) is an opaque engineering thermoplastic
formed by the copolymerization of Acrylonitrile, Butadiene, and Styrene
typically used for injection molding applications. Usually, it is composed of
half the amount of Styrene with the remaining balance divided between
Acrylonitrile and Butadiene. ABS possesses low production cost, excellent
toughness, temperature stability and solvent resistance properties superior to
those of other engineering polymers such as high impact polystyrene. The three
monomers involved in the formation of Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene play
different roles in the performance of material-while Acrylonitrile provides
chemical and thermal stability to the polymer, Butadiene enhances its
toughness and strength and Styrene imparts a nice and glossy finish. ABS finds
applications across various consumer products such as housing appliances
(refrigerator, washing machine etc.), luggage, camera bodies, battery cases,
packing crates, radio, various furniture parts, protective headgear and
musical instruments etc. ABS/PC i.e. Acrylonitrile Butadiene
Styrene/Polycarbonate blend is a thermoplastic alloy widely used in commercial
and industrial applications such as automotive, electronics,
telecommunication, etc. where hard yet lightweight and easily processed
materials are required.

EPDM (Ethylene Propylene Diene Monomer) rubber is a synthetic elastomer with a
unique combination of properties that make it suitable for a wide range of
applications. Here is a technical description of EPDM rubber. EPDM rubber is a
terpolymer consisting of ethylene, propylene, and a diene monomer, which
introduces unsaturation into the polymer structure. The diene monomer can
vary, with commonly used ones including dicyclopentadiene (DCPD) and
ethylidene norbornene (ENB). The presence of the diene monomer allows for
cross-linking, which enhances the properties of the rubber.



**The Chemical Structure of EPDM has been represented below:  **

**  
**

**\--{- [Ethylene]m---[Propylene]n----[Diene]o--}x --**



The subscripts "m" , "**n** ", and "o" represent the number of repeating units
of Ethylene, Propylene and Diene, respectively, and "x" represents the number
of chains. The diene is usually dicyclopentadiene, ethylidene norbornene, or
1,4 hexadiene. These terpolymers can be vulcanized by traditional techniques.

EPDM rubber is produced through a solution or suspension polymerization
process, where the monomers of ethylene, propylene, and diene are chemically
reacted under controlled conditions with the use of a catalyst. EPDM rubber
has excellent resistance to a wide range of chemicals, including acids,
alkalis, polar solvents, and many organic substances. It exhibits good
resistance to aging and weathering, making it suitable for outdoor
applications.



EPDM rubber exhibits excellent elasticity and flexibility, allowing it to
withstand repeated deformations and recover its original shape. It has a low
compression set, meaning it can maintain its shape and resilience even under
prolonged compression. EPDM rubber has a relatively high tensile strength and
tear resistance, providing durability and resistance to mechanical stresses.

Anisole, also known as methoxybenzene is a colorless liquid in which Benzene
is substituted by methoxy group. It is miscible in ethanol, yielding a clear
colorless solution and is prepared by ether synthesis reacting sodium
phenoxide with methyl bromide and related methylating reagents. The product
finds its applications in the manufacturing of perfumes, dyes, and
pharmaceutical products. Furthermore, it is also finding its applications as
an insect pheromone in agriculture pesticide application which is also one of
the key demand drivers for Anisole. It is mainly produced through the reaction
of methylating agent of dimethyl sulfate with phenol in alkaline aqueous
solution. In addition, Anisole is heated to react with hydrobromic or
hydroiodic, carbon-oxygen bond cleaves, phenol and halogenated methane is
produced, which is an important method for determining methoxy group of
benzene ring.

Detergent alcohols or fatty alcohols are long-chain alcohols that contain
between 12 and 18 carbon atoms. They are produced commercially from both
synthetic (mainly olefins) and natural feedstocks (primarily palm kernel oil).
Detergent alcohols are typically processed further into cleansing agents used
in products such as washing machine liquid, industrial detergent, and hair
shampoo. Naturally, Fatty Alcohols are produced by transesterification of
vegetable or animal derived triglycerides followed by hydrogenation of the
thus formed esters to alcohol. The natural oils used are mainly palm oil and
palm kernel oils (for C16-18 alcohols), coconut oil (for C12-14 alcohols) and
other natural vegetable oils (like corn, soybean etc.) may also be used. In
the synthetic route, petroleum feedstocks are made to undergo the Ziegler
process in which Ethylene is further polymerized using triethylaluminium (TEA)
as a catalyst, followed by air oxidation. The process produces even-numbered
fatty alcohols.

Tertiary Butyl Alcohol (TBA) is also known as tert-butanol or t-butanol and
possesses the chemical formula (CH3)3COH. It is an isomer of Butanol with
camphor like smell and can be found in either solid or liquid state at room
temperature. Its boiling point varies between 82°C to 83°C. TBA can be
produced by various processes like it can be produced by isobutane using
hydroperoxide process, by the hydration of isobutylene in the presence of
catalyst, and by reacting Acetone with Methyl Magnesium Chloride. TBA is used
for several industrial applications like it is used as solvent, for
denaturation of alcohol, to produce MTBE (methyl tertiary butyl ether), ETBE
(ethyl tertiary butyl ether) and TBHP (tertiary butyl hydroperoxide). It is
also used for the production of floating agents, perfumes, cosmetics etc. It
can be used as octane booster in gasoline and as an ingredient for paint
removers.

Ethylene-bis-stearamide, etc. Defoamers find applications in various domains
such as in water treatment, Food Processing and Agribusiness, chemical
manufacturing, paper and pulp, paints and coatings and others.

Nitric Acid is a colourless, highly corrosive mineral acid possessing the
chemical formula HNO3. It is highly oxidizing and very corrosive in nature and
may cause severe burns on exposure to skin. It is found in liquid form at room
temperature as its boiling point is 83°C. In industries, Ostwald process is
mainly used for the production of Nitric Acid. The working steps for Ostwald
process are as follows- first, ammonia is taken and oxidised in a chamber at
600°C which produces Nitric Oxide. Later, Nitric Oxide is treated with water
to produce Nitric Acid. Nitric Acid is majorly used for the production of
fertilizers in addition to being a key manufacturing of polyurethane (PU),
inks, plastics etc. When nitric acid is combined with HCl in a particular
ratio, Aqua regia is formed which is another corrosive solution capable to
dissolve metals like gold and platinum.

Propionic Acid or Propanoic Acid is a naturally occurring member of carboxylic
acid family. It is a saturated fatty acid with chemical formula CH3CH2COOH.
Propionic Acid has a boiling point of 141.2°C and is found in liquid state at
room temperature. In industries, propionic acid is produced by
hydrocarboxylation of ethene in the presence of a catalyst. In
hydrocarboxylation process CO (carbon monoxide) and H2O (water) reacts with
ethene in the presence of a catalyst to produce Propanoic Acid. Ni (CO)4
(Nickel tetracarbonyl) is the catalyst mostly used for this reaction. Another
method, which is not so popular in industrial manufacturing of Propionic Acid
is, oxidation of Propenal in the presence of magnesium salt at around 45°C.
There are limited number of uses of Propionic Acid like it is used as a
preservative for animal food and in human food as well, it is used to control
growth of bacteria in hay, food grains in poultry farm. It is also used to
make Cellulose Acetate Propionate (CAP) which is a thermoplastic and used to
make frames of sunglasses and spectacles etc. it is also used to manufacture
herbicides and food additives like calcium propionate and sodium propionate.

Sodium Propionate is a sodium salt of propionic acid with chemical formula
C2H5COONa. It is a white or colourless hygroscopic crystalline solid, which
means it can adsorb or absorb water molecules from surrounding. Sodium
Propionate is commercially manufactured by the reaction of Propionic Acid with
Sodium Carbonate or Sodium Hydroxide. Primarily, Sodium Propionate is used as
a preservative in different food products. It is widely utilised in bakery
products as a mould inhibiter. In addition, it is also used as a preservative
in wines, carbonated drinks, processed meats etc. Sodium Propionate is also a
food additive approved in many countries including USA, Australia, New Zealand
etc., most of the health agencies of various countries consider it as
completely safe and applies no restrictions on its use. In several industries,
Sodium Propionate is also used as an antibacterial and antifungal agent.

Hexene is an alkene with a chemical formula C6H12. The prefix "hex" denotes 6
carbon atoms in the molecule, while the "-ene" suffix denotes that there is an
alkene present in which two carbon atoms are connected through a double bond.
There are various isomers of Hexene, depending on the geometry and position of
the double bond in the chain. One of the most common industrially used isomers
is 1-hexene which is an Alpha-Olefin. Hexene is widely used as a comonomer in
the production of Polyethylene. Industrially, hexanes are widely utilized in
the formulation of glues for shoes, leather products, and roofing. They are
also used for the extraction of cooking oils (such as canola oil or soy oil)
from seeds. Other applications of Hexene include cleansing and degreasing,
textile manufacturing, additive in consumer products such as gasoline, glue,
varnishes and inks, and others. Hexene has a wide application scope in various
end-use industries including lubricants, plasticizers, intermediate chemicals,
detergent intermediates, lubricants, pulp & paper, additives, and others.

number of carbon atoms varying from 4 to as many as 22-26. These are generally
derived from natural fats and oils. The physical state of Fatty Alcohols is
highly dependent on the chain length, unsaturation or saturation and
branching. For example, stearyl alcohol is a saturated alcohol possessing 18
carbons and melting point of 58 deg. Celsius while oleyl alcohol is an
unsaturated 18-carbon alcohol possessing one double bond and melting point of
-7.5 deg. Celsius. Iso-stearyl alcohol is an 18-carbon alcohol with one methyl
branch and melting point of less than -60 dec. Celsius. Fatty Alcohols have
several commercial applications, including their use as lubricants,
surfactants, solvents, emulsifiers, plasticizers, thickeners, and even fuels.
They are the most common ingredients of personal care and home care products.
They are used in a variety of cosmetics such as as shampoo, conditioner,
shower gel, antiperspirant and lipstick. Fatty Alcohols are usually
manufactured by two processes- the first is an oleochemical process, based on
natural oils and fatty acids and the other is a synthetic route. Naturally,
Fatty Alcohols are produced by transesterification of vegetable or animal
derived triglycerides followed by hydrogenation of the thus formed esters to
alcohol. The natural oils used are mainly palm oil and palm kernel oils (for
C16-18 alcohols), coconut oil (for C12-14 alcohols) and other natural
vegetable oils (like corn, soybean etc.) may also be used. In the synthetic
route, petroleum feedstocks are made to undergo the Ziegler process in which
Ethylene is further polymerized using triethylaluminium (TEA) as a catalyst,
followed by air oxidation. The process produces even-numbered fatty alcohols.

Leatherette, also known as synthetic or faux leather, is an artificial

quality, and ease of cleaning. Leatherette is also considered an animal-

consumers. It is resistant to moisture and stains and offers a uniform finish.
However, it lacks the breathability, flexibility, and aging characteristics of
natural leather. Over time, it may crack or peel, especially under harsh
conditions. Despite this, leatherette remains a popular and practical option
for both commercial and personal use, balancing aesthetics, cost-efficiency,
and ethical considerations.

**Rosin****,** also called **colophony  **or **Greek pitch**  (Latin: pix
graeca), is a solid form of resin obtained from pines and some other plants,
mostly conifers, produced by heating fresh liquid resin to vaporize the
volatile liquid terpene components. It is semi-transparent and varies in color
from yellow to black. At room temperature, rosin is brittle, but it melts at
stove-top temperature. It chiefly consists of various resin acids, especially
abietic acid. The term "colophony" comes from colophonia resina, Latin for
"resin from Colophon," an ancient Ionic city. It becomes sticky when warm and
has a faint pinelike odour. Gum rosin consists of the residue obtained upon
distillation of the oleoresin (a natural fluid) from pine trees (the volatile
component is a spirit of turpentine); wood rosin, obtained by solvent
extraction of the stumps, is usually of a darker color.

Polypropylene Glycol (commonly abbreviated as PPG) is also known as
Polypropylene Oxide and is a polymer of Propylene Glycol. PPG shares several
common properties with Polyethylene Glycols (PEG). It is usually available in
liquid state and mostly insoluble in water above 25 deg Celsius. Polypropylene
glycol (PPG) is soluble in all concentrations with organic solids and liquids,
the key exception being straight-chain aliphatic hydrocarbons. It is generally
produced via addition of Propylene Oxide to 1,2-propylene glycol at 100-200°C
and under pressures between 2000 and 6000 hPa in the presence of alkaline
catalysts. Key applications of Polypropylene Glycol include subsiding foaming
in industrial processes and for making polyurethane resins (PU), hydraulic
fluids, and various other materials. It is also used as a surfactant, wetting
agent, dispersant in leather finishing. PPG is also in blended with
conventional polyether polyols to produce high load bearing foams for several
industrial uses.

pharmaceutical products. They aid in forming stable formulations, enhancing
drug absorption, and improving the spreadability of ointments. Tallow fatty
acids are utilized in industrial applications as lubricants, greases,
biofuels, and feedstock materials for the production of soap and biodiesel.

Diethylenetriamine (DETA) under systematic IUPAC nomenclature is also termed

hydrolysis of the amine hydrochloride salt. It is used as a curing agent for
epoxy resins. In the oil and gas industry it is used in extraction of acid
gas, sensitize nitromethane, agrochemicals and production of hydyne
(propellent for liquid fuel rocket). Global major players of DETA market are
BASF, AkzoNobel, Huntsman Corporation, Dow Chemicals, Arabian amines Company,

Liquid paraffin, also known as mineral oil, is a colorless and odorless
petroleum-derived substance with a chemical formula primarily composed of
saturated aliphatic hydrocarbons (CnH2n+2). These hydrocarbons, mainly linear
alkanes, consist of straight-chain structures with single bonds between carbon
atoms, rendering them highly saturated. Liquid paraffin finds common usage in
the pharmaceutical industry, particularly in formulating oral medications and
laxatives, where it serves as a lubricant, facilitating the passage of stool
in cases of constipation. Additionally, it is a key ingredient in various
cosmetic and personal care items like skin creams, lotions, and baby oils,
owing to its inert nature, lack of color, and absence of odor, making it well-
suited for these applications. As a byproduct of crude oil refining, liquid
paraffin emerges during the distillation process in a refinery, where crude
oil is separated into different fractions based on boiling points. The
fraction containing liquid paraffin undergoes further processing through
vacuum distillation, conducted at lower pressures to minimize boiling points
and prevent thermal degradation. In the hydrofinishing stage, a hydrotreating
process involves treating the liquid paraffin fraction with hydrogen under
high temperature and pressure. This step serves to eliminate impurities such
as sulfur and nitrogen compounds, along with unsaturated hydrocarbons.

formats. The major end use industries of Formic Acid are Agriculture, Textile

Calcium chloride is a chemical compound with the formula CaCl2. It is a
crystalline salt that is highly soluble in water. Calcium chloride is
primarily produced as a by-product of the Solvay process, which involves the

yields calcium chloride as a solution, which is further purified and processed
to obtain the desired grade. Several companies worldwide are involved in the
production of calcium chloride. Some of the prominent manufacturers include
Occidental Chemical Corporation, TETRA Chemicals, Ward Chemical, Qingdao
Huadong Calcium Producing Co. Ltd., and Solvay SA Calcium chloride finds wide
applications in various industries. It is commonly used as a de-icing agent
for roads and sidewalks during winter. In the oil and gas industry, it is
utilized for drilling fluids and well-completion operations. Calcium chloride
is also used in the food industry as a firming agent, in water treatment
processes, as a desiccant, and in the manufacturing of plastics, textiles, and
pharmaceuticals. Its hygroscopic properties make it valuable in moisture
control applications.

Fatty Acids are carboxylic acids comprising of saturated, unsaturated, or
branched aliphatic groups of different lengths. Fatty Acids are typically
produced from the splitting of palm oil which involves oil refinement followed
by its hydrolysis with high-pressure steam. Fatty acids are immiscible in
water in their acidic form, but they show high aqueous solubility as sodium or
potassium salts. The melting point of fatty acids depends on their structure.

melting point than the unsaturated carbon chain containing fatty acids. The
saturated fatty acids have high stability in comparison to unsaturated fatty
acids that tend to auto-oxidize at atmospheric conditions. Fatty acids are
enriched with emulsifying and opacifying properties that have made them
extremely popular in the personal care and cosmetics industries. They are also
perfect wetting and foaming agents which warrant their application in the
detergent sectors as well.

Levetiracetam is an anticonvulsant medication primarily used in the treatment
of epilepsy to control and prevent seizures. It is effective in managing
partial-onset seizures, generalized tonic-clonic seizures, and myoclonic
seizures in both adults and children. Levetiracetam works by modulating the
activity of neurotransmitters in the brain, although its exact mechanism of
action is not fully understood. It is believed to bind to a specific synaptic
vesicle protein (SV2A), which may inhibit excitatory neurotransmitter release
and reduce neuronal firing, thus stabilizing electrical activity in the brain.
Unlike many other anticonvulsants, Levetiracetam does not rely on the
modulation of GABA (gamma-aminobutyric acid) or sodium channels. Its side
effects are generally mild and can include dizziness, fatigue, irritability,
and, in some cases, mood changes or psychiatric symptoms such as depression or
aggression. It is available in oral and intravenous forms, providing
flexibility in both outpatient and hospital settings. Levetiracetam has a
relatively favorable pharmacokinetic profile, as it is rapidly absorbed and
has minimal protein binding, with a half-life of about 6 to 8 hours, making it
suitable for both monotherapy and adjunctive therapy in various seizure
disorders. Additionally, it does not require routine blood level monitoring,
further enhancing its ease of use. However, as with all antiepileptic drugs,
it requires careful consideration of potential interactions with other
medications and individual patient factors to optimize therapy.

Diammonium Phosphate (DAP) is a water-soluble phosphate compound having IUPAC
name Diammonium hydrogen phosphate and chemical formula (NH2) HPO4. It is
produced by the reaction of Ammonia with Phosphoric Acid at around 100°C.

granules, and then sieved to get the required product. DAP is one of the
largely used phosphate fertilisers globally. It is always advised to not to
use DAP with alkali chemicals, because of the tendency of ammonium ion to
convert into Ammonia at a higher pH. DAP is widely used as a fire retardant to
combat with forest fire, it is a viable part of commercial firefighting
products. In addition, there are many other uses of DAP like it is used as a
yeast nutrient in alcoholic beverages, in some cigarettes to enhance nicotine,
as a soldering flux etc.

Disodium phosphate dihydrate (Na₂HPO₄*2H₂O) is a white, crystalline powder or
granular substance that is odourless and highly soluble in water, with a
typical purity of 98-99%. It has a melting point of around 70°C and dissolves
in water to form a mildly alkaline solution, making it an essential reagent in
various industrial, pharmaceutical, and commercial applications. In industrial
settings, disodium phosphate dihydrate is primarily used as a buffering agent,
pH regulator, and dispersing agent. It plays a critical role in the
formulation of cleaning agents, water treatment systems, and detergents by
stabilizing solutions and controlling pH levels. In the food industry (E339),
it is commonly used as an acidity regulator and dispersing agent in processed
foods, beverages, dairy products, soft drinks, and processed meats. It helps
maintain texture, stability, and pH balance, and ensures uniform consistency
in powdered mixes and baking applications. In the pharmaceutical sector,
disodium phosphate dihydrate is used as an excipient in injectable and oral
formulations, helping to stabilize active ingredients, enhance solubility, and
maintain pH levels. It is also used in the production of vaccines, where its
buffering capacity is essential for maintaining the efficacy of the active
compounds. Additionally, disodium phosphate dihydrate is used in the
production of ceramics and glass as a fluxing agent. Proper storage in
moisture-resistant containers is essential to prevent degradation.

and separation stages. The resulting glyoxal product finds application in
textile industries for fabric finishing, as a cross-linking agent in paper
manufacturing, and in pharmaceuticals and cosmetics for various formulations.

Pet coke or Petroleum Coke is solid carbon, majorly produced as by product in
crude oil-refining process. Physical and chemical properties of pet coke are

than natural gas/naphtha and hence is a significant choice for production of
chemicals. Over the past few years, pet coke has emerged as a promising
alternative to the conventional sources of energy such as coal, naphtha and
natural gas for production of various chemicals and intermediates. Pet coke
has high carbon percentage and low ash content as compared to other sources,
which makes its useful as feedstock.

Petroleum resins are thermoplastic polymers that are amorphous produced by the
polymerization of unsaturated hydrocarbons. The feedstock are various by-
products of naphtha crackers. These resins have typically a low molecular
weight ranging from about 400 g/mol to 5000 g/mol. The main types are- C5
aliphatic, C9 aromatic and C5/C9 resins. Aliphatic C5 Resins are monomers made
from C5 piperylene and its derivatives. These resins are polymerized to
oligomeric resins with low to high softening point. They are available in a
wide range of molecular weights (MW) and softening points (solid grades 85 -
115°C and liquid grades 5 - 10°C) and provide outstanding tack. They also have
a light yellow to light brown color and possess excellent heat stability.
Aromatic C9 Resins** ** are made from C9 aromatic hydrocarbons. Their
composition depends on the hydrocarbon feedstock (coal tar and crude oil).
These resins are available in a wide range of softening points. Compared to C5
resins, they have a much higher melt viscosity, are of darker color (dark
yellow to brown)and have a higher softening point ranging from about 100 to
150°C.C9 resins are very versatile resins that are compatible with many
polymers.

Polyoxymethylene (POM), also referred as Acetal, Polyacetal and
Polyformaldehyde was discovered by Hermann Staudinger in 1920, but back then
it was not thermally stable enough to be used as it was an engineered
thermoplastic. Thermally stable Polyoxymethylene was discovered by Stephen Dal
Nagore who figured that reacting the ends of Hemiacetal with Acetic Anhydride
can transform the depolymerized Hemiacetal into a thermally stable plastic.
The final product formed had high strength, hardness, and rigidity, thus it
could be used in insulators, bobbins, and connectors. Besides, its high
thermal stability and in toxicity makes it favorable to be used in insulin pen
and metered dose inhaler in pharmaceuticals industry. Polyoxymethylene can be
produced commercially with the help of anhydrous formaldehyde.

Paints and Coatings, Adhesives and Sealants, Chemicals, Plastic additives,
Textiles, Paper and Inks and Others. Among these, Paints and Coatings is the

Polyacrylamide (PAM) is a water-soluble polymer, physically available as a
white crystalline solid. It is a non-ionic compound which forms strong
hydrogen bonds with water molecules and hence capable to retain water. This
water absorbing and retention quality makes it suitable to be used as a
superabsorbent. Commercially, PAM is produced by hydration of Acrylonitrile
(ACN) to produce Acrylamide and then cross-linking polymerization of
Acrylamide that produces PAM. During production, Acrylamide is always advised
to be handled with care due to its high toxic nature, although after
polymerization polyacrylamide become non-toxic. When PAM is dissolved in water
it forms gel like structure and hence shows flocculant properties. Due to this
property, it is widely utilised for water treatment and sewage cleaning
purposes. Apart from that, it is also used in paper making, and as a chemical
intermediate for the production of other chemical products.

Urea also known as Carbamide, is an organic compound with chemical formula

ideal affinity for water. Commercially, Urea is manufactured by reacting
synthetic ammonia with carbon dioxide. Urea finds wide application in
agriculture industry, where more than 90% of total Urea produced in the world

nitrogen content among most used nitrogenous fertilizers. Urea also finds its

Urea-formaldehyde resins and Urea-Urea formaldehyde where latter is used in
marine plywood. In addition , Urea has been commonly used in automobile
industry to reduce the NOx pollutants in exhaust gases from combustion of
diesel, dual fuel, and natural gas .

Ethylene Carbonate (EC) is an organic compound having chemical formula
(CH2O)CO. It is a colourless/transparent crystalline solid with melting point
of around 35°C and hence found solid at room temperature. Commercially,
Ethylene Carbonate is manufactured by the reaction of feedstock Ethylene Oxide
(EO) with Carbon Dioxide to produce EC. Although, on laboratory scale it can
be produced by the reacting Urea with Ethylene glycol. There are many direct
and indirect applications of Ethylene Carbonate, but it is mainly used as an
electrolyte solution in lithium-ion batteries. Apart from that EC is used as
polar solvent for many other applications, as a plasticizer, as a precursor to
produce Vinyl Carbonate which is further utilised for inorganic synthesis and
making polymers. In addition, EC is utilised for the synthesis of aliphatic
polyurethane, glycerol carbonate, dimethyl carbonate etc. and also as a
lubricant, soil hardening agent, and electrolyte for capacitor etc.

Paraformaldehyde (PFA) is a polyoxymethylene which is also called polyacetals.
It is a polymer of Formaldehyde with 8-10 degree of polymerisation. Production
of PFA starts from taking aqueous solution of Formaldehyde of about 40% to 55%
purity. This solution is then concentrated up to 85%, followed by condensation
and dewatering. Condensed solution is later taken out for polymerisation and
drying in a special drying equipment. In the final step, after cooling
Paraformaldehyde is formed. PFA is widely used for manufacturing resins, like
Phenolic resins, Amino resins and many other surface coating resins. In
addition, PFA is used in paper industries for coating, in leather industry for
making chemical preservative and in fertilizers industries. PFA is also used
for pest control and as a disinfectant in industries as well as in homes.

Silane is an inorganic compound having chemical formula SiH4. It is a toxic
gas with highly repulsive smell which is similar to acetic acid. Silane can be
poisonous for humans if inhaled and can create irritation and burns if one
comes in contact with open skin or mucous membrane. Silane is also highly
flammable in nature and can be ignited in air. There are several procedures to
manufacture Silane, one of them is by reacting Magnesium Silicide with
Hydrochloric Acid to produce silane and a by-product Magnesium Chloride.
Another method is by reacting elemental silicon with Hydrochloric Acid which
is a longer process, and it forms an intermediate compound called
Trichlorosilane at first step. This compound is converted into Silane and
Silicon Trichloride. It has several industrial applications, but majorly it is
utilised in semiconductor manufacturing industries. It is a precursor of
silicon and hence it is widely utilised in electronic industries to
manufacture products like photovoltaic modules. in addition, it is also
utilised to produce amorphous silicon for glass.

Sodium Hypochlorite is a sodium salt of hypochlorous acid and is widely known
as the oldest. Anhydrous Sodium Hypochlorite decomposes rapidly when kept at
standard temperature and pressure and the decomposition is accelerated by CO2
in the air. To keep it stable, it is either manufactured as crystalline
pentahydrates or is maintained as an aqueous solution, whereas both of them
requires refrigeration. There are several methods available to commercially
manufacture Sodium Hypochlorite. First one being the Chlorination of Sodium
Hydroxide which is a redox reaction. Second method is proceeded by reacting
Calcium Hypochlorite with Sodium Carbonate, this method is majorly used in
making hospital antiseptics. Another method is done by electrolysis of brine
solution, which produces Chlorine gas and Sodium Hydroxide, then they are
mixed to form Sodium Hypochlorite. Major applications of Sodium Hypochlorite
include its usage as a bleaching agent for household, to remove dental strain,
crockery strain etc. and most importantly as a disinfectant to clean
contaminated areas in hospitals and other areas.

Triethylamine (also abbreviated as Et3N) is a colourless compound with
chemical formula N(CH2CH3)3. It's a volatile liquid with smell like ammonia,
having melting point of -114.7°C, hence found as liquid at room temperature.
Triethylamine is produced by the reaction between Ammonia and Ethanol in
presence of heat and pressure. It is primarily utilised for the synthesis of
quaternary Ammonia compounds like ammonium salts of dyes etc. Triethylamine is
widely used as an intermediate compound for manufacturing pesticides,
medicines and many other chemicals. It is widely used in Swern oxidation
process, where it is used as an organic base to convert primary or secondary
alcohol into aldehyde or ketone. It can also be used as a catalyst during
manufacturing of Polyurethane foam, epoxy resin, in some dehydrogenation
reactions, and as an acid neutralizer for condensation reactions. In addition,
sometimes Triethylamine is also utilised as a propellent, hardening agent for
polymers etc.

Benzoyl Chloride, also known as benzenecarbonyl chloride is an organochlorine
compound possessing the formula C7H5ClO/ C6H5COCl. It is a fuming colourless
liquid with a pungent odour. It belongs to the class of Acid Chlorides. Acid
Chloride is an organic compound having a chlorine atom attached to an acyl
group. Its formula is usually written R-COCl, where R is an alkyl chain. They
are reactive derivatives of carboxylic acids and have lower boiling and
melting points. Acid chlorides can be produced from Thionyl Chloride through
nucleophilic acyl substitution reaction. Benzoyl chloride can be produced via
partial hydrolysis of benzo-trichloride and acetyl chloride can be produced by
the reaction of acetic anhydride with hydrogen chloride. Benzyl chloride is
widely utilized as a chemical intermediate in the production of certain dyes
and pharmaceutical products and as a photographic developer. It is primarily
utilized to produce Benzoyl Peroxide and is used as an intermediate to
manufacture dyes, surfactants, perfumes, pharmaceuticals.

Phosphorus Acid is a chemical compound which is manufactured by hydrolysis of
acidic anhydride or Phosphorus trichoride with steam or water. Phosphorus Acid
is an Acid containing Phosphorus and the substance equation is H3PO3. The
IUPAC name of this compound is Trihydroxide phosphorus. It is a triprotic acid
since it can deliver three protons (hydrogen particles) in an aqueous medium.
The Acid has higher acridity comparing to phosphoric acid and accordingly is
more acidic than its counterpart. The compound is significantly utilized
underway of PVC stabilizer, such as lead phosphite, engineered strands,
organophosphorus pesticides, proficient water treatment specialist and
furthermore and also it is used as strong reducing agent.

steam to produce Phosphorus acid.

  

**PCl3 + 3 H2O -> H3PO3 + 3 HCl**

  

Hence, due to such applicability, major sectors like automotive, construction,
textile and agriculture forms the major user of Phosphorus acid. Factors like
growing construction activities, increase in production volume of automotive
and high demand for clothing & apparel items are driving the growth of global

acne symptoms. Several end-use industries that utilize Zinc Powder are food

Having the chemical formula HOC(CH2CO2H)2, Citric Acid is an organic compound
that is a weak acid with no color. In citrus fruits, it naturally exists.
Citric acid is produced in more than two million tonnes annually. It is
frequently employed in various end-user industries as an acidifier, flavoring,
and chelating agent. It is most frequently used as a flavor and preservative
in food and beverages, particularly soft drinks and candies because it is one
of the stronger edible acids. To prevent the crystallization of sucrose in
caramel or to keep fats from separating in ice cream, citric acid can be used
in recipes in place of fresh lemon juice. Numerous effervescent formulations
combine citric acid and sodium bicarbonate for personal care products and
ingestible forms (such as powders and tablets) (e.g., bath salts, bath bombs,
and cleaning of grease).

helps blend oil and water, improve texture, and extend shelf life -- often
found in baked goods, whipped toppings, and ice creams. In cosmetics and
supplements, it can serve as a moisturizer or delivery agent for other
ingredients. GMS is generally considered safe and is approved for use by

Nitrochlorobenzene refers to a group of isomers comprising ortho- (2-), meta-
(3-), and para- (4-) nitrochlorobenzene, with the molecular formula ClC₆H₄NO₂.
Ortho-nitrochlorobenzene is a yellow crystalline solid with two reactive
functional groups, making it a versatile intermediate in the synthesis of
compounds such as o-nitrophenol, 2-chloroaniline, o-aminophenol, and azo dyes.
It is widely used in dyestuff, pigments, specialty chemicals, agrochemicals,
and pharmaceutical intermediates. Para-nitrochlorobenzene is commonly employed
in the production of rubber antioxidants and is synthesized by the nitration
of chlorobenzene. A significant use of this isomer is its condensation with
aniline to form 4-nitrodiphenylamine, a key intermediate in chemical
manufacturing.

C9 Solvents hydrocarbons are a series of organic molecules that form planar
ring bonds. C9 aromatic hydrocarbon resins are classically named because they
are defined by the number of carbon monomers in chemistry. Aromatic
hydrocarbons with characteristic aroma and characteristic Gardner color from 6
to 10 (dark yellow to dark brown). They are insoluble in water, light
alcohols, and ketones but soluble in aliphatic hydrocarbons and chlorinated
hydrocarbon solvents. Aromatic hydrocarbons are used mainly in adhesives,
printing inks, sealants, polychloroprene rubber, concrete curing agents,
drying agents, and paints. They are compatible with SBR, SIS, SEBS, and SEPS
and can be used as pressure-sensitive adhesives, hot melt adhesives, and
neoprene. They can also be applied to coating ships, vehicles, and bridges, as
they improve gloss, increase hardness and make areas more water resistant. In
the printing industry, petroleum resin will increase water repellence, solvent
consumption, and drying resistance. They are also used to mark hotlines. The
end-user market for this product is the coatings, coatings, and rubber
industry.

Ammonium Nitrate is a white granular solid, which is highly soluble in water
and hygroscopic in nature. It has a chemical formula NH4NO3, with a melting
point of 169˚C and highly favourable in agriculture sector. Ammonium Nitrate
is predominantly used as a fertilizer either as stand-alone product or after
blending with other like Urea Ammonium Nitrate (UAN). Industrial production of
Ammonium Nitrate includes the reaction of anhydrous Ammonia gas and
concentrated Nitric acid. This is a highly exothermic reaction which yields a
solution with 83% concentration, water is evaporated to get more than 95%
concentration, which later processed and granulated. Uzbekistan followed by
Poland, USA, Ukraine and Canada are the major producers of Ammonium Nitrate.

Polyalphaolefin (PAO) fluids are the most common major synthetic base oils
that are widely used in industrial and automotive lubricants. These synthetic
hydrocarbons are designed to provide superior lubrication performance over a
wide range of operating-temperature than petroleum oils and typically are less
volatile. PAO is industrially manufactured through a synthetic chemical
process that originates from ethylene. Ethylene is produced by cracking either
natural gas or crude oil. PAOs are extensively used in automotive fluids as
well as hydraulic, gear and bearing oils, working in extremely cold climates
or hot applications. One application in which they have not worked well is in
high-temperature (high-pressure) reciprocating air compressors due to the
valve deposits issue.

Boron Trifluoride (BF₃) is a colorless, toxic gas with a pungent odor. It is a
pivotal compound in the field of inorganic chemistry, known for its strong
Lewis acid properties. BF₃ is highly reactive and forms complexes with many
organic and inorganic molecules. Boron Trifluoride is typically produced by
reacting Boron Oxide (B₂O₃) or Boric Acid (H₃BO₃) with Hydrofluoric Acid (HF).
The primary reaction involved is:

  

B2O3+6HF->2BF3+3H2O

  

Boron Trifluoride (BF₃) has diverse applications due to its strong Lewis acid
properties. In industrial catalysis, it facilitates crucial reactions such as
Friedel-Crafts alkylation and acylation, essential for synthesizing complex
organic molecules. The petroleum industry uses BF₃ in alkylation processes to
produce high-octane gasoline by transforming smaller alkyl groups into
branched hydrocarbons. In addition to chemical synthesis, BF₃ plays a
significant role in producing fluorinated compounds and acts as a reagent in
various chemical preparations. Its industrial applications extend to the
manufacture of synthetic polymers and adhesives, where it enhances
polymerization reactions. In analytical chemistry, BF₃ is used to detect
specific functional groups in organic compounds. Overall, BF₃'s ability to
form complexes and its reactivity make it invaluable across sectors including
refining, polymer production, chemical synthesis, and analytical applications.

2-Ethylhexanoic Acid (chemical formula C8H16O2) is a carboxylic acid

production of several industrial chemicals serving plethora of downstream
applications. It is added in esters for manufacturing Polyvinylbutyral (PVB)

as an intermediate in pharmaceutical preparations. 2-Ethylhexanoic acid is
industrially produced from Propylene, which is hydroformylated to produce
butyraldehyde. Aldol condensation of the butyraldehyde produces

2-ethylhexanal yields 2-Ethylhexanoic Acid.

Nonylphenol Ethoxylates (NPE) are nonionic surfactants that are industrially
synthesized by the polymerization reaction between ethylene oxide and
nonylphenol. Depending on the reaction conditions, the polymerization reaction
yields a mixture of compounds having ethoxy ether chains of varying lengths.

which range from being clear to foggy colorless liquids or white colored
solids. The hydrophilicity of NPE is defined by its mole value where up to 6
moles of NPEs can stay dispersed in water, 7 moles or above NPEs quickly get
dissolved in water and other organic polar solvents. Displaying high
hydrophilic-lipophilic balance (HLB), NPEs are outstanding emulsifying and
dispersing agents. This unique property of NPEs makes them suitable for
application in cleaning agents, cosmetics, textile and leather processing,
agricultural chemicals.

Polybutylene adipate terephthalate (PBAT) is a biodegradable thermoplastic
polyester that possesses a combination of properties suitable for various
applications. It is a copolymer formed by the polymerization of four monomers:
1,4-butanediol (BD), adipic acid (AA), terephthalic acid (TA), and dimethyl
terephthalate (DMT). The structure of PBAT consists of repeating units derived
from these monomers. The polymer chain contains segments of butylene glycol
(BG), adipic acid, and terephthalic acid or dimethyl terephthalate. The BG
units provide flexibility and elongation to the polymer, while the adipic acid
and terephthalic acid/dimethyl terephthalate units contribute to its strength
and rigidity.



**The chemical structure of PBAT can be represented as follows:**

**  
**

**-(BD-BG-AD-TPA/DMT)-**



where BD represents 1,4-butanediol, BG represents butylene glycol, AD
represents adipic acid, and TPA/DMT represents terephthalic acid or dimethyl
terephthalate.

Hot Rolled Coil (HRC) is the most dominantly finished steel form in the global
steel industry and the foundation for many steel-based industrial products.
Hot-rolled coil steel is a type of steel that has been roll-pressed at
elevated temperatures-over 1,600 °F, above the recrystallization temperature
for most steels. This makes the steel easier to form, resulting in more
accessible work products. The billet is first heated and then sent for
flattening through large rollers for HRC manufacturing. Here, rolled coils are
kept at a high temperature and run through a series of rollers to achieve
their finished dimension. Rolled steel is spun into coils and left to cool for
sheet metal. Hot-rolled coil steel is highly malleable and cost-efficient.
China, Japan, India, and Russia are the top exporters of the hot-rolled coil.
Railroad tracks, shipbuilding, automotive, and construction projects often use
hot-rolled coil steel.

Recycled Linear Low-Density Polyethylene, often abbreviated as R-LLDPE, is
derived on recycling of LLDPE, a thermoplastic polymer which is a petroleum-
derived product having short-branched chains. The recycling process involves
the recovery of LLDPE from post-consumer used mixed bales from the dumping
area. The LLDPE from collected plastic wastes are separated based on density
difference and sorted on the basis of color variations. The segregated
products are shredded into flakes by grinding after which they are sent for
cleaning to do away with any kind of contamination. The cleaned flakes are
subjected to high temperatures for melting in a single-screw extruder during
which the remaining contaminants are removed by melt filter. The cooled
product is sent for pelletization to produce pellets that are usable by the
downstream industries. R-LLDPE typically find usage in the films and packaging
industry.

Hydrogen generated from renewable sources is termed as "Green Hydrogen." It is
a clean energy source and emits water vapors, and does not leave behind any
residue like conventional fuels. It can be generated by water splitting
through Electrolysis, Thermolysis, or Photolysis. Industrially water
electrolysis is done by three methods, i.e., PEM, Solid Oxide, and Alkaline.
PEM produces high-quality Green Hydrogen. In the PEM Electrolysis method, the
solid polysulfonated membranes are used as an electrolyte. The thermodynamics
behind the splitting of water into Hydrogen and Oxygen is the energy required
is the same time as the energy released during the formation of water
molecules. The obtained product must reduce carbon emissions by at least
60-70% to be certified as green one. Green Hydrogen is mixed with Natural Gas
to produce Green Ammonia, which is used to make fertilizers. The gas is also
used as a fuel in cars and airships.

metals, which prevents corrosion and interferes with conductivity. Copper is
less oxidative and has lower resistivity. Metals with low resistivity will
have higher conductivity. Copper wire and cable are used in power generation,
transmission, distribution, telecommunications, electronic circuitry, and

Galvanized Plain Sheet is an ordinary steel sheet that has been zinc-coated to
make it corrosion resistant. Regular steel is made of iron, which rusts when
exposed to moisture, such as rain or humidity in the air. Galvanized Steel
Sheet is steel that has been coated with a thin layer of zinc to offer
corrosion protection for items like garbage cans, storage tanks, and
construction structures. Before galvanizing, steel must usually be cold-
rolled. Galvanizing is a zinc coating or layer applied to steel sheets using a
process known as "continuous hot-dip," which involves passing the steel sheet
through a bath of molten zinc. On both sides of the sheet, the liquid zinc
links to the iron in the steel, providing a protective coating. Galvanized
steel sheet is commonly used as roofing materials in homes, businesses, and
industries.

Aramid fiber is a high-performance synthetic fiber characterized by its
remarkable strength-to-weight ratio, heat resistance, and durability, making
it a vital material in various demanding applications. Developed in the 1960s,
aramid fibers, such as Kevlar and Nomex, exhibit exceptional tensile strength,

resistance to chemicals and abrasion further enhances their utility, allowing
them to be used in manufacturing tires, ropes, and various industrial
components. As a result, aramid fibers have become synonymous with high-
performance materials, delivering both safety and reliability in environments

Levodopa, also known as L-DOPA, is a medication commonly used in the treatment
of Parkinson's disease and other movement disorders, such as dopamine-
responsive dystonia. It is a precursor to dopamine, a neurotransmitter that
plays a crucial role in coordinating movement. In patients with Parkinson's
disease, the brain's ability to produce dopamine is impaired due to the
degeneration of dopaminergic neurons, leading to symptoms like tremors,
rigidity, bradykinesia (slowness of movement), and postural instability.
Levodopa is administered orally and is absorbed by the body, where it crosses
the blood-brain barrier and is converted into dopamine in the brain. This
helps to replenish dopamine levels, alleviating motor symptoms. However,
levodopa is often combined with other medications like carbidopa, which
prevents its premature conversion to dopamine outside the brain, thus
enhancing its effectiveness and reducing side effects such as nausea. Despite
its benefits, long-term use of levodopa can lead to complications like motor
fluctuations (on-off phenomenon), where the effectiveness of the drug may
become unpredictable, and dyskinesia, which are involuntary, erratic
movements. Levodopa remains one of the most effective treatments for
Parkinson's disease, but its use requires careful management to balance its
therapeutic effects with potential side effects.

industrial and chemical applications. Chemically, it is an amine and an
alcohol, with the molecular formula C₂H₇NO. It is primarily employed as a
versatile intermediate in the synthesis of surfactants, detergents, and
emulsifiers, due to its ability to interact with both hydrophobic and
hydrophilic substances. MEA also serves as a key component in the production
of various pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals, and is used in gas treatment
processes to remove carbon dioxide and hydrogen sulfide from natural gas and
refinery gases. Its role in the manufacture of cosmetics and personal care
products highlights its importance in both industrial and consumer sectors.
However, despite its usefulness, MEA must be handled with care, as it can be
irritating to the skin, eyes, and respiratory system, necessitating
appropriate safety measures during its use and storage. The major key players
operating in the global TEA market are BASF, Dow Chemical Company, Huntsman,
INEOS, Xianlin, Nippon Shokubai, SABIC, AkzoNobel, Jinyan, Zhongxin Chemicals,
Xian Lin Chemical & Jiangsu Yinyan Specialty Chemicals etc.

Sulfamethoxazole is a bacteriostatic sulfonamide antibiotic. It is effective
against both gram-negative and positive bacteria. It is generally given in
combination with trimethoprim, a dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor, which
inhibits the reduction of dihydrofolic acid to tetrahydrofolic acid. The
chemical formula of Sulfamethoxazole is C10H11N3O3S. Sulfamethoxazole is a
structural analog of para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA). Sulfamethoxazole can be
prepared by reacting 3-amino-5-methylisoxazole with para-
acetamidobenzenesulfonyl chloride. The acetyl group is then cleaved to yield
Sulfamethoxazole. Sulfamethoxazole is an isoxazole (1,2-oxazole) compound. It
inhibits a critical step in bacterial folate synthesis. Sulfamethoxazole is
useful for treating various bacterial infections, including urinary,
respiratory, and gastrointestinal tracts.

Fluorspar is a mineral form made of calcium and fluorine (CaF2). It is
utilized in several chemical, metallurgical, and ceramic processes.
Hydrothermal processes lead to the deposition of Fluorspar in veins. It
frequently appears as a gangue mineral mixed with metallic ores in these
rocks. Some dolomites and limestones also contain fluorite in their cavities
and cracks. The chemical industry uses acid-grade Fluorspar, which is highly
pure. CaF2 makes up more than 97 percent of it. Even though it is employed in
lower grade applications, most Fluorspar used in the United States is acid
grade. It is primarily utilized in the chemical sector to create hydrofluoric
acid (HF). The HF is then employed to produce a wide range of goods, such as
fluorocarbon compounds, foam blowing agents, refrigerants, and fluoride
chemicals.

tissue disorder. It helps in the reduction of fever too. It is commonly used
as a substitute for Aspirin.

Lisinopril is an active pharmaceutical ingredient that is used to produce
Lisinopril drugs. It has a molecular formula C21H31N3O5. Lisinopril is a

tablet, capsule, and suspension. The drug obtained from Lisinopril API has an

output when used after acute myocardial infarction. The kidney problems in
people with diabetes mellitus are also prevented using Lisinopril. It is
active ingredient in products such as Lisinopril Dihydrate, Lisinopril
Sulfate, Lisinopril Maleate, Hydrochlorothiazide.

Lopinavir is an active pharmaceutical ingredient with the molecular formula
C37H48N4O5. It is available in the white to light tan powder form. The
finished drug from Lopinavir API acts as an antiretroviral protease inhibitor
which, in combination with other antiretroviral used to treat human
immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection and AIDS. It is a peptidomimetic
molecule with a hydroxy ethylene scaffold that simulates the peptide linkage
generally attacked by the HIV-1 protease enzyme but cannot be degraded,
blocking HIV-1 protease activity. It is also considered in the treatment of

somewhat soluble in isopropanol, and practically insoluble in water. End users
who require Lopinavir include pharmacies, hospitals, and clinics. It is an
active ingredient in products like Kalerate, Lopinavir/Ritonavir Mylan.

Sodium chlorite is a compound used for water disinfection and purification. It
is produced in large quantities as flakes or a solution from chlorine dioxide
and sodium hydroxide. Its use as a bleach for textiles was first discovered
during the 1920s. Today, sodium chlorite is an important specialty chemical
with sales over $18 million annually. In its dried state, sodium chlorite
(NaCl O2 ) is a white or light yellow-green solid. The greenish tint comes
from trace amounts of CdO2 or iron, which are production residuals. It is sold
in solution or as a solid. The technical grade is made up of about 80% sodium
chlorite and the rest is sodium chloride. Large scale production is based on a
reaction of chlorine dioxide in a sodium hydroxide solution. Hydrogen peroxide
is also present as the reducing agent. Sodium chlorite is manufactured in
three phases, chlorine dioxide production, sodium chlorite generation, and
recovery.

Silicone rubber is a synthetic elastomer that is composed primarily of
silicon, oxygen, carbon, and hydrogen. It is a versatile material known for
its excellent thermal stability, electrical insulation properties, and
resistance to extreme temperatures, chemicals, and weathering. Silicone rubber
is commonly used in a wide range of industries, including automotive,
electronics, aerospace, healthcare, and construction.
